Whenever people ask me for relationship advice, I always hear all this awful stuff about the other party and everything they do wrong. I usually tell the person that they need to step back and keep one very important thing in mind: your partner is not you. They have their own personality and reasons for thinking things, so if you're trying to address a problem you should be trying to look at it not just from their shoes but with their eyes, not yours.

You listed a lot of things going wrong in the relationship, and because of that everyone here is primarily going to tell you that she's awful and you should leave her. It's easy for someone to take that position when you only list the bad things, but I'll try to offer you some advice that will help you work through this stuff.

I'm divorced (years ago) and we both have a child of our own.

This is a red flag which you didn't elaborate on. I'm assuming you're implying that she's never been married, and had her child out of wedlock. On the one hand this means that she might not be the most careful person or easy to be in a committed relationship with, but on the other hand it tells me that she would probably have some serious fears of abandonment. Perhaps in her past relationship she constantly heard compliments, but then when the person up and leaves she suddenly feels that they were all lies? How can she easily trust anyone after that? Think about how something like that would affect your ability to trust what people say.

One of the main problems is that she is always accusing me of lying, she doesn't accuse me of cheating or anything but its constantly when I pay her a compliment or when I say something random like "oh hey I was just thinking about you" I'll say that and she'll say "yeah whatever"

This is odd, but here's a question: are you lying? Is there any merit to this statement? As guys we're often terrified of dealing with the emotional landslide that comes from a misplaced comment, but there is something to be said for total honesty. More than once my girlfriend has freaked out because I made a comment about her makeup, or outfit, or w/e, but she also loves it when I compliment her because she knows it's genuine. Maybe you should try to withhold your compliments somewhat, only tell her something if you feel like it's really true--and when she'll know also it's really true. Don't tell her she's beautiful when her makeup is half-done, but if you know that she spent a lot of time putting together an outfit or picking a nail color, compliment her on it.

The other aspect of this is it gets to the trust issue I mentioned before. It sounds like she has some serious trust issues, and she's become a bit jaded to white compliments. It might be good to try to have a serious discussion with her about why she doesn't believe what you say. If you don't address this, it's going to be a huge problem down the road.

That brings me to the second issue, anytime I bring something up that's bothering me she thinks its either bullshit or she just doesn't want to hear it, that will then will usually turn into some sort of argument because it pisses me off as I feel like shes not taking what I'm saying seriously.

It's never acceptable for someone to blow off their partner's concerns or problems, but I'd encourage you to ask yourself how often do you do this. Girls hate guys who are emotionally needy, and I'll be honest a big reason my relationship goes so smoothly is because I almost always keep problems to myself. My gf sees me as stalwart and dependable, and in the very rare occasions that I open up to her she takes me very seriously.

My only advice, as awful as it sounds, is to just try to tone it back a bit. The only thing worse than a needy girl is a needy guy. Ultimately it's up to you to judge if her emotional support is lacking or not, since I really don't know how serious these problems you're discussing are, but if it's just something about how someone was a jerk at work or how bad traffic was, just keep it to yourself.

3rd issue, anytime something doesn't go how she planned it, its my fault. She wanted me to take her home the other night but we both fell asleep, next morning she blames me for it...

It sounds like she's not very responsible, and is probably depending on you to be the responsible one. Yeah, it's not really your fault, but you're also going to seem like such a charmer (not to mention a man with a spine) when you take charge and tell her that you're taking her home, or not letting her do something that's going to cause a problem later.

Be a man and take responsibility. It may not be your responsibility to take, but it will make her absolutely love you for it, and ideally she'll start reciprocating more.

Last issue, she's constantly texting/calling me. I don't have a major problem with this but here's the thing, if I start texting her or calling her and she decided that day that she's too busy for whatever reason then it's a problem and "we don't need to txt/talk all the time. This happens consistently when she's around her family. It's like all of the sudden shes not bored anymore so fuck what I'm trying to talk about...

This is important to address, but you're also reading into it too much. If you're texting her when she's with her family, that's a stupid move. Treat it like a break, you don't have to be in constant communication. She's going to appreciate you letting her focus on her family, and you should appreciate getting some time to yourself.

As for her constantly texting you...dude, that's what girls do. Women, young ones especially, get their social value entirely from how much people pay attention to them. She's going to be texting you and trying to get attention because if you ignore her she's going to feel like you're really not that into her.

I think with the texting you're both just being unreasonable, you know? She isn't bored anymore because she's with her friends/family/whatever, so what's wrong with that? When you're about to hang out with friends would you like it if your gf was texting or calling you? Of course not, it would be rude. Just sit down with her and address it, work out some simple rules about when she shouldn't be texting you and when you shouldn't be texting her.

Any advice? If any of you have been in the same situation I'd love to hear about it.

Never ask someone for relationship advice if they've been in the same situation, since ultimately every relationship is defined by the personalities and experiences of the people involved. Solutions need to be catered to the situation.

The best advice I can offer you is that it sounds like she's not really respecting, appreciating, or trusting you. If you really love her, then you need to think about how you can address the problems that she obviously has with you before you start asking her to address your complaints. Relationship is all about give-and-take, and sometimes it's up to you to be the one who gives first. If you make serious effort to address these problems and she's not making any effort to address yours, then come back and ask for advice again--but it sounds like there's a lot that you could be doing to make things easier for her, so you should try that first and see how her behavior changes as a result.
